01Museum Booster, Vienna — Communication Strategy

Don’t Panic

Launch strategy for the Museum Booster Academy

How do you launch a leadership platform for museum leaders in a sector defined by shrinking budgets, political pressure, and quiet panic — without adding to the panic? At Museum Booster in Vienna I built the launch communication strategy for the Museum Booster Academy: four peer-based intensive workshops for museum leaders and middle management. The core concept, “Don’t Panic”, answers the sector’s mood with strategic reassurance instead of urgency.

0campaign phases
0two-day workshops
0seats per cohort
0professionals in reach
The campaign — nine phases of trust

What I did

  • Built the communication plan end to end: DESTEP, Porter’s Five Forces, and 7S analysis translated into a nine-phase launch strategy.
  • Ran a large-scale LinkedIn discussion on museum leadership toward 2030 and gathered practitioner interviews at trade fairs — the base for the audience analysis and persona.
  • Shaped the “Don’t Panic” concept and channel mix — landing page, LinkedIn, newsletter, webinar, merch — with budget and a KPI framework tied to workshop capacity.

What the research showed

  • Museum leaders operate under structural budget pressure and public scrutiny; panic has quietly become a driver of decisions.
  • Leadership programmes compete on trust, legitimacy, and peer credibility — not on content.
  • Leaders want confidential, peer-based sense-making — not another training promising quick fixes.

Strategy grounded in Uncertainty Reduction Theory and Cialdini’s principles of social proof and authority — each phase lowers perceived risk before asking for commitment.

02What Matters Platform, Vienna — Events & Communication

Future Bridge

Talk series — culture, design and foresight

Future Bridge is a Vienna talk series by the What Matters Platform, connecting culture, design, and foresight through conversations that matter. Across three events I did the communication, planning, promotion, content creation, photography, and on-site coordination. What I did

  • Communication, planning, and promotion for three Future Bridge events — through to on-site coordination and photography.
  • Built the content side: key visuals, social content, and personalised postcard-style emails for recurring guests after Milan Design Week.
  • Supported speakers and partners on site — from a marketing trend-report talk to Good Plastic Company’s material showcase.

What it taught me

  • Events work as platforms for niche professional communities — preparation and atmosphere decide whether real exchange happens.
  • How to translate a major international context, Milan Design Week, into a smaller community conversation in Vienna.
  • Event coordination is a living process: plans change fast, and the network carries you.

Part of a year of cultural events work in Vienna — alongside a Ukrainian Embassy event during Eurovision week, the most intense coordination work of the year.

03Fontys × Deloitte — Campaign

Tomorrow’s Leadership in Art

Workplace-bullying campaign

A campaign against workplace bullying, aimed at misogynistic behaviour among Gen X men in leadership at Dutch companies. The concept is a traveling art exhibition backed by Deloitte, built from art, a VR simulation, and DEI workshops. Instead of lecturing people, it works on self-image and social identity in a professional setting.

What I did

  • Led the desk research on workplace power dynamics and gender-based bullying.
  • Built campaign assets: the Facebook ad, the event website, and the merchandise concept, each shaped around behaviour-change theory.
  • Helped design the intervention and the interactive exhibition, and worked the psychology into the communication.

What the research showed

  • Bullying falls hardest on women.
  • Most of it comes from people who hold power.
  • Gossip and passive aggression get normalised.

04Fontys × Lumosa — Strategy

Sustainability You Can Trust

Communication plan for Lumosa

A positioning and communication plan for Lumosa, an energy-tech company doing LED lighting and EV charging, ahead of their 2025 trade fairs. Their B2B buyers, mostly municipalities in Noord-Brabant, want technical proof, not warm storytelling. We kept the brand’s warmth but backed it with data, under the line “Sustainability You Can Trust”.

What I did

  • Led audience and persona work with DESTEP and stakeholder interviews.
  • Ran the competitor analysis against Signify, Shell Recharge, and Fastned.
  • Set positioning and wrote tone of voice and platform guidelines for LinkedIn, Instagram, and trade fairs.

What we found

  • Engineers and municipalities want factual, technical communication.
  • Lumosa read as warm but thin on proof: no white papers, no data.
  • Competitors stood out on scale and tech transparency.

Picked to present the plan to the client, who singled out the slogan.

05Fontys × Living Lab 040 — Strategy

The Conscious Toolkit

Communication strategy for Living Lab 040

Living Lab 040 is an urban district in Eindhoven testing sustainable housing, community building, and ecological infrastructure. Most of its research sat in dense reports. We repositioned it as an approachable platform and built a toolkit that turns the research into things professionals can actually use.

What I did

  • Split the strategy for two audiences: community-facing creative engagement, and technical sharing for industry and academics.
  • Built a toolkit of ready-to-use AutoCAD templates (street layouts, green roofs, modular housing) and Revit/BIM models.
  • Tied it together with a self-explanatory website.

The gap

  • Low awareness of LL040, inside the field and out.
  • Research locked in dense, academic formats.
  • North Brabant audiences prefer informal, social engagement.

About

I’m Sasha Pertseva. I work in communication and events in the cultural sector, and I’m finishing a degree in International Communication Management at Fontys in Eindhoven. Over the past year I’ve been in Vienna — at Museum Booster on the communication, editorial, and event side of museum and design programmes, and with the What Matters Platform on cultural events. The “Don’t Panic” launch strategy and the Future Bridge series above both come out of that year.

The remaining projects are from earlier work at Fontys. The through-line is the same: take something research-heavy and make it land with real people.
